stages.title: State-space filtering and nowcasting: research guide
stages.html:
State-space filtering and nowcasting

Estimate latent states and update them as noisy releases arrive.

The Kalman filter weighs prior and measurement uncertainty; a real-time nowcast must also respect release dates and data vintages.

Workflow. Update a latent-state estimate by balancing prior and measurement uncertainty.

Diagnostic: Inspect innovation, Kalman gain, and covariance recursion. The main failure to avoid is a state estimate that ignores signal-to-noise information.

stages.title: Kalman filtering intuition lab
stages.note: Run the Kalman recursion on a latent random-walk state — raise the measurement variance to shrink the gain (trust the prior, smooth) or raise the process variance to grow it (chase each release).
stages.template:
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 200; R = {{R}}; Q = {{Q}}
state = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, np.sqrt(Q), n))   # latent random-walk state
obs = state + rng.normal(0, np.sqrt(R), n)        # noisy measurements
x_hat = np.zeros(n); x_hat[0] = obs[0]; P = 1.0
gains = np.zeros(n)
for t in range(1, n):
    x_pred = x_hat[t-1]; P_pred = P + Q            # predict step
    K = P_pred / (P_pred + R)                      # Kalman gain
    x_hat[t] = x_pred + K*(obs[t] - x_pred)        # update on innovation
    P = (1 - K)*P_pred                             # covariance recursion
    gains[t] = K
rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((x_hat - state)**2))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 3.6))
ax.plot(obs, '.', color='#c9c6ac', ms=3, label='noisy obs')
ax.plot(state, color='#4f8fba', lw=1.6, label='true state')
ax.plot(x_hat, color='#da9100', lw=1.6, label='Kalman estimate')
ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.set_title(f'steady-state gain={gains[-1]:.2f}   RMSE={rmse:.2f}')
plt.tight_layout()
print(f'R(measure var)={R:.2f}  Q(process var)={Q:.2f}  steady-state gain={gains[-1]:.3f}')
print('High R -> low gain -> trust prior (smooth); high Q -> high gain -> chase the data.')

stages.title: State-space filtering and nowcasting: worked Python model
stages.note: Run the reproducible example, then change one assumption and compare the output.
stages.code:
prior_mean, prior_var = 1.2, 0.9
measurement, measurement_var = 2.0, 0.4
gain = prior_var / (prior_var + measurement_var)
posterior_mean = prior_mean + gain*(measurement-prior_mean)
posterior_var = (1-gain)*prior_var
print(f"Kalman gain: {gain:.3f}")
print(f"Posterior state: {posterior_mean:.3f}")
print(f"Posterior variance: {posterior_var:.3f}")

expected_mean = prior_mean+expected_gain*(measurement-prior_mean)
assert abs(gain-expected_gain) < 1e-10
assert abs(posterior_mean-expected_mean) < 1e-10
print("grader: Kalman update is correct")

stages.title: Nowcasting with state space: model decision
stages.note: A team is about to report results without checking release calendar, ragged edge, and real-time vintages.

steps.prompt: What is the best next action?
choices: Align mixed-frequency releases and update estimates only when new information arrives.
Increase decimal precision and report immediately.
Drop observations until the preferred coefficient appears.
steps.explain: The defensible workflow is to align mixed-frequency releases and update estimates only when new information arrives.

steps.prompt: Which risk should the final report address explicitly?
choices: Only whether the sample mean is positive.
look-ahead bias from revised or not-yet-released observations
Whether every coefficient has the same sign.
steps.explain: The relevant failure mode is look-ahead bias from revised or not-yet-released observations.
